title: Define quantile sentinels and graded degradation policy for Optimize
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Problem: Current Optimize eval gating relies on aggregate mean deltas and fixed thresholds which miss distributional regressions (long-tail failures) and does not provide a graduated response strategy. This ticket defines (1) a quantile-based sentinel framework to detect degradation in distribution tails and critical prompt cohorts, and (2) a graded degradation / rollback policy that maps detected signal severity to automated mitigation actions (soft degrade, traffic-shepherding, immediate rollback). Scope: PRD covers sentinel definitions, statistical test choices, minimum sample sizes, A/B power targets, integration points with Console alerts and Rollouts, and runbook actions. Out of scope: instrumentation changes to model runtime (handled in ENG-23755) and embedding-level drift detection (separate follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel taxonomy defined: Tier-0 (core prompts, must-pass), Tier-1 (high-impact cohorts), Tier-2 (long-tail quantiles). Each tier has a clear owner and sample set composition method.
Quantile-based checks implemented: facility to compute per-prompt and cohort 90th and 95th percentile error/score deltas between baseline and candidate with historical smoothing window configurable.
Composite degradation score: define formula combining mean delta, 95th-quantile delta, and incidence rate of failures; documented and agreed by ENG and Research.

Statistical decision rules: provide explicit multiple-testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg by default with Bonferroni as opt-in), significance thresholds (default alpha=0.01 for Tier-0, alpha=0.05 for Tier-1), and minimum sample sizes computed for 90% power to detect 1.5% absolute win-rate change in A/B.
A/B criteria: experiments must meet minimum N or be flagged as underpowered; platform enforces a soft block preventing full rollout from canary unless power criteria satisfied or PM approves.

Automated mitigation mapping: for severity levels (low, medium, high) define automated actions: low -> reduce traffic weight by 30% + monitoring, medium -> route 50% to baseline + notify on-call, high -> automatic full rollback to previous stable model and open incident ticket with links.
Console integration: dashboard widgets for sentinel heatmap, cohort sample counts, p-values, composite score, and a one-click rollback button wired to rollout automation.
Runbook: detailed steps for on-call to triage a Tier-0 trigger, including reproducibility checks, sample replay links, relevant GitHub PRs and contextual logs.
Docs: PRD and short runbook published in Confluence; internal announcement template for customers affected by high-severity rollbacks.
End-to-end test: synthetic canary that injects known regressions across 1k sentinel prompts reproduces expected detection and mitigation in staging within configured SLAs.
notes: Design decision: prefer quantile signals to catch long-tail regressions rather than only mean-based tests; accepted trade-off of higher sample requirements for higher confidence in tails.

Statistical library decision: ENG prefers a lightweight server-side implementation using existing stats package; Research recommends providing a reference Jupyter notebook for auditability and offline analysis.
Risk: increasing sensitivity to tail regressions may increase false positives; mitigation includes progressive thresholds, smoothing windows, and manual override by PM/Eng.
Cross-team dependencies: needs Console work (CON-1821) for dashboard widgets and Rollouts work (ENG-2902) for traffic-shepherding APIs.
Customer impact classification: Tier-0 failures map to high customer impact; Tier-1 medium; Tier-2 low but actionable for continuous improvement.
